LESSON: POPULATION DISTRIBUTION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Population
Topic 2.2: Population Distribution

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Population Distribution. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How is population spread out in the county?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe patterns of population distribution in the county
2. appreciate population distribution in the county

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: POPULATION DISTRIBUTION
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Population Distribution helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: POPULATION DISTRIBUTION
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Describe patterns of population distribution in the county

What this means
In this part you learn to describe patterns of population distribution in the county. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe patterns of population distribution in the county.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Population Distribution” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe patterns of population distribution in the county. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate population distribution in the county

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate population distribution in the county. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate population distribution in the county.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Population Distribution.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate population distribution in the county. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Population Distribution is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Population Distribution” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: describe patterns of population distribution in the county)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Population Distribution. (skill: appreciate population distribution in the county)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Population Distribution to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe patterns of population distribution in the county.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate population distribution in the county.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Population Distribution from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Population Distribution: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Population Distribution?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How is population spread out in the county?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Population Distribution means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe patterns of population distribution in the county.
5. Be able to: appreciate population distribution in the county.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
